WT306WorkshopHandoutMenopauseandMentalHe: Everything  about menopause is terrible, I shouldn't have to deal with this!

Negative thoughts about menopause can be totally understandable, especially if your culture views menopause negatively or you have difficult symptoms. Mental fitness can help you navigate those negative thoughts in ways that support healthy coping.
Let’s explore some mental fitness strategies that can help.

Radical acceptance can help us drop the struggle between how we wish reality was compared to how it is. No amount of wishing will stop a hot flash, for example, or make menopause go away. Deciding to accept that menopause is present will help decrease the added stress of wishing it were different, and help us make space for healthy coping.

When thoughts show up that are overly negative, overestimate threat, or underestimate your ability to cope, consider rebalancing your thinking using your mental filter. 
In a kind and curious tone, ask yourself questions from the list below to help you challenge and rebalance your thinking:
Am I overestimating the possibility of something bad happening?
Am I underestimating my coping abilities?
What would I say to a close friend who had this thought?
You

You can use your answers to these questions to help you create a more balanced thought, which can benefit mood and boost your mental well-being. 
For example, “I’m so sweaty. Everyone is going to think I’m disgusting.” might become, “I’m probably noticing my symptoms more than everyone else.”
MenopauseOlivier.Handbook.Culturecan: Culture can shape our perceptions and experiences of menopause. In some cultures, menopause is seen as a time of renewal and regeneration. In others, it can be seen as the end of a person’s prime, something to be feared or stigmatized.
MenopauseOlivier.Handbook.Group30800.Men: Menopause, and the transition into and out of it, can be tough—physically, mentally, and emotionally.   And menopause often arrives at a time when life is already full of change. You could be caring for aging parents, watching children leave home, navigating evolving relationships, taking on more responsibilities at work—or maybe even all of the above, which can cause added stress.

MenopauseOlivier.Handbook.Group30965.But: But no matter the cultural context, the menopausal time of life can bring stress and challenges. One of the best ways to cope with this stress and meet these challenges is by investing in your mental well-being.
